absent: Locking discipline around early page table and logical map updates is not shown in these fragments.
Detailed layout of page table descriptors and firmware device structures is not defined here.
Exact numeric values of address bounds, masks, shifts and sizes are not stated.
Behavior when firmware description lacks boot processor entry or contains no usable memory is not fully shown.
Interaction with secondary processor bringup beyond logical map construction is not shown.
Full error handling for malformed reserved memory descriptions beyond ramdisk case is not shown.

findings.text: Global early initialization routines for fixed mapping, physical memory, input output remapping, error detector shadow, and paging are provided for boot sequencing by higher level orchestration.
CPU topology discovery from firmware description builds logical to physical identity mapping while reserving logical zero for boot processor.
Early fixed address window setup walks page table hierarchy from top to leaf, creating missing intermediate tables from reserved storage.
Main physical memory initialization selects aligned base, clips memory beyond linear reach while keeping kernel image reachable, and registers kernel and firmware tables as reserved.
Early input output remapping initialization is a thin delegation to generic setup logic.
Paging activation maps physical memory, permits allocator resizing, installs identity mapping, and declares kernel virtual areas in sequence.
Hardware identifiers outside allowed mask and repeated identifiers are ignored rather than assigned, preserving uniqueness of logical map.
Boot processor identity must appear once in firmware description and is recorded without consuming a fresh logical slot, with repeat appearance treated as error.
Fixed mapping population is idempotent, touching only absent entries and leaving already present entries undisturbed, with leaf index derived from address and level shift.
Linear region size follows virtual address width with a reduced cap when running under hypervisor mode on very large address hardware.
Initial ramdisk is retained only when fully enclosed by usable linear range; otherwise it is disabled with a warning, and when retained it is reserved for later use.
Crash kernel reservation is inactive unless the corresponding build option is present and command line parsing succeeds, delegating actual reservation on success.
Direct memory access limits combine firmware provided caps with low memory presence, falling back through progressively wider defaults when narrower zones are absent.
Page table descent for shadow uses on demand allocation, selecting static early tables during bootstrap and dynamic zeroed pages otherwise, with leaf pages prefilled to a defined poison value.
Detection recursion depth for the initial task starts cleared.

Linear mapping applies tagged attributes for allocation tag support, isolates kernel text alias for later permission tightening, and shrinks each range inward to avoid overlapping adjacent unmapped guards.

Boot memory sequencing runs early destructive test, publishes page frame bounds, then initializes distance topology, hypervisor reservation, DMA limits, contiguous reservation, crash reservation, and final dump in order.
Memory error detector initialization proceeds from shadow mapping to depth reset to generic activation, leaving tag based modes for later dedicated steps.

Shadow memory construction preserves early coverage via temporary root, clears prior range with edge aware handling, then populates kernel image, gap, and physical memory shadows before restoring main root.
Sharing of top level entry between kernel mapping and fixed mapping is unexpected and constrained to a particular page size configuration, otherwise treated as fatal.
Failure to obtain backing storage for shadow tables aborts boot immediately rather than continuing with incomplete coverage.
Overlap of top level index between direct map end and dynamic area start is forbidden, enforced as a build time check, with special note for reduced address space configurations.
